## Abstract

This tutorial compares the tree inferred in Tutorials 1 and 2 with four published phylogenies of Cactaceae.
A supermatrix tree is one estimate of the phylogeny; taxon sampling, choice of loci, substitution models and inference method can all change the topology.
Comparison with independent trees shows which relationships are shared and which differ.

The reference trees are those of Amaral *et al*. (2022), Thompson *et al*. (2024), Zuntini *et al*. (2024) and de Vos *et al*. (2025); the last two are based on hundreds of nuclear genes.
The trees are compared with the Robinson-Foulds distance (Robinson & Foulds 1981) and the Different Phylogenetic Information distance (Smith 2020), and the distances are projected into tree space by multidimensional scaling (MDS).

## Complete Pipeline Execution Workflow

### Module 13: Comparison with Published Phylogenies

#### Reference Trees

The four reference trees are those of Amaral *et al*. (2022), Thompson *et al*. (2024) and Zuntini *et al*. (2024), and a species tree estimated with `ASTRAL-III` from the gene trees of de Vos *et al*. (2025).
They are not distributed with the package: the licences of three of them are not established, and one route serves the four.
The user obtains each tree from its source, saves the four in one folder under the names below, and sets the path of the folder in `~/.Renviron` as `PHYLOCACTUS_REFERENCE_TREES`.
The comparison also reads the checklist of Cactaceae (Korotkova *et al*. 2021) from the local path in `PHYLOCACTUS_CHECKLIST` (`phylocactus_checklist()`; Tutorial 1).

| File in the folder | Study | Source (DOI of the study) | File of the study |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reference_amaral_2022.tree` | Amaral *et al*. (2022) | <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.biocon.2022.109677> | `Tree_80MD.tre` |
| `reference_thompson_2024.tree` | Thompson *et al*. (2024) | <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-51666-2> | `ultra_cacti_JT.tre` |
| `reference_zuntini_2024.tree` | Zuntini *et al*. (2024) | <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07324-0> | the Cactaceae of the Kew Tree of Life, release 4.0 |
| `reference_devos_2025_astral.tree` | de Vos *et al*. (2025) | <https://doi.org/10.1007/s00606-025-01948-z> | `ASTRAL-III` species tree from the gene trees of the study (below) |

Figure 1 and Table 1 of this page are drawn from the outputs of the reference run distributed with the package (the tree-space coordinates and the pairwise distances), so the page is built without the reference trees and without the checklist (Korotkova *et al*. 2021).
Paths to external software and to data obtained by the user are read from environment variables.

#### Species Tree from the Gene Trees of de Vos *et al*. (2025)

Gene trees estimated from multilocus and target-capture data often disagree.
Part of this discordance has biological causes, such as incomplete lineage sorting and hybridization, and under high levels of incomplete lineage sorting a concatenated analysis can be statistically inconsistent (Kubatko & Degnan 2007).

`ASTRAL-III` (Zhang *et al*. 2018) estimates a species tree from a set of unrooted gene trees under the multispecies coalescent, by finding the species tree that shares the largest number of quartets with the gene trees.
The `ASTRAL-III` Java archive (`.jar`) must be downloaded separately.

#### Paths in `.Renviron`

Store paths to local software and data in `~/.Renviron`.
Shared scripts then contain no local paths.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# Add these lines to your ~/.Renviron file (e.g., using usethis::edit_r_environ())
# PHYLOCACTUS_REFERENCE_TREES="/path/to/reference_trees"
# PHYLOCACTUS_CHECKLIST="/path/to/CactaceaeFullList_2026_07_01_Beatriz_Merino.xlsx"
# ASTRAL_PATH="/path/to/astral.5.7.8.jar"
# DEVOS_GENETREES_PATH="/path/to/QC.bestTreeCollapsed.trees"
# DEVOS_METADATA_PATH="/path/to/606_2025_1948_MOESM1_ESM.csv"

# Read them in R:
reference_dir <- Sys.getenv("PHYLOCACTUS_REFERENCE_TREES")
astral_jar <- Sys.getenv("ASTRAL_PATH")
gene_trees_file <- Sys.getenv("DEVOS_GENETREES_PATH")
metadata_file <- Sys.getenv("DEVOS_METADATA_PATH")
```

#### Running `ASTRAL-III`

de Vos *et al*. (2025) sequenced the Angiosperms353 loci.
The reference tree used here is the `ASTRAL-III` species tree estimated from their gene trees, after the tip labels are converted to species names with the sample metadata of the study.

The chunk below renames the tips of the gene trees, writes them to a file, and runs `ASTRAL-III`.
With `run_astral_locally <- FALSE`, the default, it copies the species tree saved in the folder of reference trees instead.
Output files are written to a temporary directory; change `val_dir` to keep them.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# Target output paths in the validation directory
val_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "10_Validation")
dir.create(val_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
output_tree <- file.path(val_dir, "QC.Species_tree_astral.tree")
renamed_gene_trees_file <- file.path(val_dir, "QC.Species_tree_astral_rename.tree")

# Set to TRUE to run ASTRAL-III; FALSE (default) copies the precomputed tree.
run_astral_locally <- FALSE

astral_jar       <- Sys.getenv("ASTRAL_PATH")
devos_gene_trees <- Sys.getenv("DEVOS_GENETREES_PATH")
devos_metadata   <- Sys.getenv("DEVOS_METADATA_PATH")

java_bin <- Sys.which("java")
if (!nzchar(java_bin) && file.exists("/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk/bin/java")) {
  java_bin <- "/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk/bin/java"
}

if (run_astral_locally && nzchar(astral_jar) && file.exists(astral_jar) && 
    nzchar(devos_gene_trees) && file.exists(devos_gene_trees) && 
    nzchar(devos_metadata) && file.exists(devos_metadata) && 
    nzchar(java_bin)) {
  
  meta <- read.csv(devos_metadata, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
  meta$species_name <- gsub(" ", "_", meta$`Scientific name`)
  meta$Sample_from_tree <- stringr::str_extract(meta$`Name in tree`, "P[0-9]+")
  
  map_sample <- setNames(meta$species_name, meta$Sample_from_tree)
  map_srr    <- setNames(meta$species_name, meta$`ENA run acc.`)
  
  gene_trees <- ape::read.tree(devos_gene_trees)
  
  rename_tips <- function(tree) {
    tips <- tree$tip.label
    paftol_to_sample <- function(x) {
      num <- stringr::str_extract(x, "[0-9]+")
      paste0("P", stringr::str_sub(num, -5))
    }
    sample_ids <- ifelse(stringr::str_detect(tips, "PAFTOL"), paftol_to_sample(tips), NA)
    species_vec <- ifelse(stringr::str_detect(tips, "PAFTOL"), map_sample[sample_ids], map_srr[tips])
    species_vec[is.na(species_vec)] <- tips[is.na(species_vec)]
    tree$tip.label <- species_vec
    return(tree)
  }
  
  gene_trees <- lapply(gene_trees, rename_tips)
  class(gene_trees) <- "multiPhylo"
  ape::write.tree(gene_trees, file = renamed_gene_trees_file)
  
  cmd <- paste(shQuote(java_bin), "-jar", shQuote(astral_jar), 
               "-i", shQuote(renamed_gene_trees_file), 
               "-o", shQuote(output_tree), "2>/dev/null")
  system(cmd)
} else {
  # Copy the de Vos et al. (2025) species tree saved in the folder of reference trees
  ref_devos <- file.path(Sys.getenv("PHYLOCACTUS_REFERENCE_TREES"), "reference_devos_2025_astral.tree")
  file.copy(ref_devos, output_tree, overwrite = TRUE)
}
```

### Topological Comparison

The focal tree is the chronogram from Module 10, whose topology is that of the maximum-likelihood tree (all 1205 bipartitions shared).
`validate_phylogenies()` restricts every tree to Cactaceae and to the names accepted in the checklist (Korotkova *et al*. 2021), then computes pairwise distances on four taxon sets:

- **A1:** species shared by all trees;
- **A2:** species shared by the focal tree and the trees of Thompson *et al*. (2024) and Amaral *et al*. (2022);
- **A3:** all species in the genera shared by all trees;
- **A4:** one species per genus shared by all trees.

Two distances are computed for each pair of trees.
The normalized Robinson-Foulds distance (RF) is the proportion of bipartitions that are not shared by the two trees.
The Different Phylogenetic Information distance (DPI) also gives partial credit to bipartitions that are similar but not identical.
Both are computed on unrooted trees.
Each distance matrix is projected onto two dimensions by classical MDS; trees that lie close together have similar topologies.

**Rooting.** `validate_phylogenies()` roots every tree on *Leuenbergeria*.
The Module 10 chronogram is rooted on Talinaceae, but the family filter removes all terminals outside Cactaceae, and *Leuenbergeria* is sister to the rest of the family in the focal tree.
The genus can be changed with `rooting_genus`; trees without it are left unrooted and flagged in `SUPP_rooting_summary`.
Because RF and DPI are computed on unrooted trees, the rooting affects only the exported tree files, not the distances or the tree-space projection.

**The constraint.** The focal tree was inferred under the topological constraint of Module 8 (Tutorial 2), so part of its agreement with each reference is imposed by the constraint and not found by the data. On each shared taxon set, 12 to 17 of the bipartitions the focal tree shares with a reference are imposed by the constraint: 27 to 37 % of the shared bipartitions in the small sets A1 and A4, where the deep splits weigh most, and 5 to 8 % in the large sets of Thompson *et al*. (2024) and Amaral *et al*. (2022). The table below gives, for the reference run, the published RF beside the RF without the constrained bipartitions, removed from both trees of the pair. Every distance rises, by 0.010 to 0.100; for example, the RF of A1 against Zuntini *et al*. (2024) rises from 0.254 to 0.312. The order of the references by distance does not change in A1, A2 and A3, and in A4 Zuntini *et al*. (2024) and Thompson *et al*. (2024) exchange places (0.470 and 0.467). DPI cannot be split this way, because it gives partial credit across bipartitions, and is reported with the constraint only. Tutorial 2 weighs the constrained bipartitions absent from each reference by the support of the reference clades that contradict them: the two nuclear trees contradict none at the level of a tribe with support, while Amaral *et al*. (2022) contradicts with support three relationships at that level, the position of Rhipsalideae in core Cactoideae II (bootstrap 87), Tephrocacteae with Opuntieae (100) and core Cactoideae I with II (99).

| Set | Reference | Shared terminals | Imposed and in the reference | RF | RF without the constrained bipartitions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Zuntini | 66 | 14 | 0.254 | 0.312 |
| A1 | Thompson | 66 | 12 | 0.381 | 0.449 |
| A1 | Amaral | 66 | 12 | 0.429 | 0.510 |
| A1 | de Vos | 66 | 14 | 0.270 | 0.333 |
| A2 | Thompson | 620 | 14 | 0.554 | 0.564 |
| A2 | Amaral | 620 | 17 | 0.645 | 0.661 |
| A3 | Zuntini | 119 | 15 | 0.440 | 0.490 |
| A3 | Thompson | 734 | 14 | 0.628 | 0.638 |
| A3 | Amaral | 631 | 17 | 0.678 | 0.696 |
| A3 | de Vos | 88 | 15 | 0.353 | 0.420 |
| A4 | Zuntini | 78 | 15 | 0.387 | 0.470 |
| A4 | Thompson | 78 | 12 | 0.413 | 0.467 |
| A4 | Amaral | 78 | 14 | 0.493 | 0.593 |
| A4 | de Vos | 78 | 14 | 0.360 | 0.424 |

**What each reference can test.** The tree of Zuntini *et al*. (2024) is built on a constrained backbone of at most five samples per family, so its deep relationships within Cactaceae are not an independent test of the constraint (Tutorial 2). The tree of Thompson *et al*. (2024) carries no support values and its chronogram is not independent of Ramírez-Barahona *et al*. (2020), whose ages anchor the chronogram of this package; it is a comparison tree only, and a distance to it says nothing on the support of a conflict.

**Trees compared.** The four reference trees are read from the folder in `PHYLOCACTUS_REFERENCE_TREES`. The focal tree is the chronogram produced in Module 10, `8_Dating/dated_summary_hpd.tree`. When that file is absent, as when this tutorial is run on its own, the reference chronogram distributed with the package (`phylocactus_chronogram_hpd.tree`) is used instead.

The chunk below runs the comparison on the user's machine. Figure 1 and Table 1 are then drawn from the tree-space coordinates and the pairwise distances of the reference run, distributed with the package (`phylocactus_table_tree_space.csv`, `phylocactus_table_tree_distances.csv`); `plot_tree_space()` draws the figure that `validate_phylogenies()` returns.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(PhyloCactus)

# The focal tree is the chronogram of this run; the reference trees and the checklist are read from
# local paths (PHYLOCACTUS_REFERENCE_TREES, PHYLOCACTUS_CHECKLIST).
focal_tree <- file.path("8_Dating", "dated_summary_hpd.tree")
if (!file.exists(focal_tree)) {
  focal_tree <- system.file("extdata", "phylocactus_chronogram_hpd.tree", package = "PhyloCactus")
}
reference_dir <- Sys.getenv("PHYLOCACTUS_REFERENCE_TREES")
tree_paths <- list(
  FocalTree   = focal_tree,
  Zuntini     = file.path(reference_dir, "reference_zuntini_2024.tree"),
  Thompson    = file.path(reference_dir, "reference_thompson_2024.tree"),
  Amaral      = file.path(reference_dir, "reference_amaral_2022.tree"),
  deVos       = file.path(reference_dir, "reference_devos_2025_astral.tree")
)

# Drop trees whose files are missing
existing_trees <- tree_paths[sapply(tree_paths, function(x) nzchar(x) && file.exists(x))]

if (length(existing_trees) > 1) {
  checklist_file   <- phylocactus_checklist()
  constraints_file <- system.file("extdata", "cactus_constraints.csv", package = "PhyloCactus")

  # validate_phylogenies() harmonizes tip names, computes RF and DPI distances,
  # and projects them into tree space.
  validation_outputs <- validate_phylogenies(
    trees_mapping_list = existing_trees,
    checklist_csv = checklist_file,
    constraints_map = constraints_file,
    out_dir = file.path(tempdir(), "10_Validation")
  )
  validation_outputs$plot
} else {
  message("Set PHYLOCACTUS_REFERENCE_TREES to the folder of the reference trees to run the validation.")
}
```

```{r, fig.width=11.69, fig.height=8.27, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.cap="**Figure 1.** Tree space of the focal chronogram and the four published phylogenies: classical MDS of the normalized Robinson-Foulds (RF) distances, one panel per taxon set (A1 to A4); trees close together have similar topologies."}
library(PhyloCactus)

# Tree-space coordinates of the reference run (SUPP_tree_space_coordinates.csv of Module 13)
tree_space <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "phylocactus_table_tree_space.csv", package = "PhyloCactus"))
plot_tree_space(tree_space, metric = "RF")
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Pairwise distances of the reference run (TABLE_pairwise_tree_distances_main.csv of Module 13)
dist_table <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "phylocactus_table_tree_distances.csv", package = "PhyloCactus"))
knitr::kable(head(dist_table), caption = "Table 1. Pairwise tree distances: normalized RF and DPI for each pair of trees and taxon set (first rows).")
```

`TABLE_pairwise_tree_distances_main.csv` lists the distances for every pair of trees and every taxon set, and `FIG_tree_space_main.pdf` shows the tree-space projections.
The distances summarize overall agreement between topologies; they do not identify which clades are in conflict.

## Conclusion

This tutorial completes the core workflow of `PhyloCactus`: assembly of a multilocus supermatrix from GenBank, maximum-likelihood inference with bootstrap support, divergence time estimation with penalized likelihood, integration of IUCN Red List data, figures, and comparison with published phylogenies.

The second branch of the package, molecular identification by DNA barcoding, builds a reference library of Cactaceae from the same `phylotaR` mining, measures how well it tells genera and species apart, and identifies a sample against it (Tutorials 5 and 6).

[Continue to Tutorial 5: Molecular Identification of Cacti (DNA Barcoding)](https://beeamerino.github.io/PhyloCactus/articles/tutorial-5-cactus-phylogeny-barcoding.html)
